title: Making Knowledge Distillation Cheap Enough to Run at Scale
hook: Distillation is expensive mostly for two boring reasons: the teacher hogs memory, and the KL loss materializes a huge vocab-by-sequence matrix. Fix both and a four-GPU job fits on one.
key_points: Two engineering changes, no new algorithm: cache the teacher offline, and compute the KL loss in chunks.
Offline distillation precomputes the teacher's top-100 logits once, so the teacher never has to sit in GPU memory during training.
A fused chunked KL loss processes the sequence in pieces and recomputes in the backward pass instead of storing the full matrix.
Reported peak memory at 32K tokens drops from 85.2 GiB to 5.45 GiB — a 15.6x reduction.
Step time falls 5x (57.0s to 12.23s) and per-GPU throughput rises from 74.2 to 345.7 TFLOP/s; GPT-OSS 20B at 32K context fits one H200.
Their 3.2B student landed within 9 points of its 8B teacher on MMLU.
content_html: Multiverse Computing's Antonio Tiene and Iker García-Ferrero make a nice point: knowledge distillation isn't expensive because of anything deep about the idea — it's expensive because of two implementation details. The teacher model occupies GPU memory alongside the student, and the KL-divergence loss between them naively builds a matrix the size of the vocabulary times the sequence length. Remove both and the bill collapses.
extra_html:
Their two fixes are unglamorous and effective. Offline distillation runs the teacher once over the data and caches its top-100 logits per token; training then reads those from disk, so the teacher never needs to be resident. A fused chunked KL loss walks the sequence in chunks and recomputes intermediates in the backward pass instead of storing them — paying a little extra compute to avoid the big allocation.

The numbers they report: at 32K tokens, peak memory drops from 85.2 GiB to 5.45 GiB (15.6x), step time from 57.0s to 12.23s, and per-GPU throughput from 74.2 to 345.7 TFLOP/s. GPT-OSS 20B at 32K context becomes a single-H200 job rather than a four-GPU one, and their 3.2B student stayed within 9 points of its 8B teacher on MMLU. The broader claim is about who gets to do this at all — distillation as something small teams iterate on cheaply, not an enterprise-scale capital expense. Full write-up and details on the Hugging Face blog.

related.title: Distilling the Knowledge in a Neural Network
related.hook: A big model's softened probabilities say more than hard labels - they reveal how classes relate, so training a small model to mimic them transfers knowledge a one-hot target never could.

related.title: Sequence-Level Knowledge Distillation
related.hook: Match the teacher's whole output sequence, not just word-by-word probabilities, and the student translation model can drop beam search while running about 10x faster.

flashcards.prompt: Why does classic distillation need so much GPU memory?
flashcards.back_html: The teacher and student both sit in memory, and the KL loss materializes a full vocabulary-by-sequence-length matrix of logits.

flashcards.prompt: What does "offline distillation" change about the training loop?

choices.text: The teacher's top-100 logits are cached once, so the teacher isn't loaded during training
The student trains on hard labels instead of soft probabilities
Teacher and student are trained jointly in the same backward pass

flashcards.explanation_html: Precomputing the teacher's top-100 logits turns the teacher into a fixed dataset, freeing all the memory it would otherwise occupy.

flashcards.prompt: How does the fused chunked KL loss trade compute for memory?
flashcards.back_html: It processes the sequence in chunks and recomputes intermediates during backprop rather than storing them — the classic recompute-vs-store trade.

flashcards.prompt: Per the post, what practical setup change did these optimizations enable for GPT-OSS 20B at 32K context?

choices.text: A single H200 replaces a four-GPU setup
Training moves from GPU to CPU entirely
The context window can be extended past 1M tokens

flashcards.explanation_html: Peak memory fell from 85.2 GiB to 5.45 GiB, which brought the job inside one H200 instead of four GPUs.
